recipes.name: Ann’s Rice Pilaf
ingredients_raw: 0.25 teaspoon Greek seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Dissolve chicken bouillon in water in a bowl.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir vermicelli pieces until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
Pour bouillon mixture into the skillet with the vermicelli.
Stir rice, black pepper, salt, and Greek seasoning into the vermicelli mixture and bring to a boil. Cover and reduce heat to low; simmer until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ann’s Rice Pilaf
raw_recipe.description: Golden bits of vermicelli pasta add a toasted flavor to this quick pilaf. Use your favorite seasoning in place of Greek seasoning, if desired.

review.reviewBody: Not too bland, not too bold, just right - and for my turkey dinner tonight that means it was perfect. Hubs and I both appreciated its simplicity. I used orzo for the broken vermicelli and chicken broth rather than the bouillon and water. Even tho’ the submitter encourages using your choice of seasoning, I stuck to the Greek seasoning as the recipe was written. As she said, however, the recipe is versatile so it allows the flexibility to use any number of different herbs or seasonings. We loved it, plain and simple.

Amazing rice recipe! along all that was listed -changed it up a bit and sautéed left over cold rice in wok with a bit of olive oil and tablespoon of butter add 1 tsp of garlic, sprinkle of red chilli pepper and paprika for colour, Italian herbs like rosemary, basil,oregano and add to oil and onion and sautéed till clear then added the left over approx 2 cups of cooked cold rice and vermicelli and fried until some rice was crisp on med heat. My family wants me to keep making it...they love it!

I use orzo and add about 1/4 cup chopped mushrooms and 1/4 cup chopped onion as soon as the orzo is becoming golden. I also add some minced garlic and parsley and saute right before adding the rice and liquid. VERY GOOD. I could only find Cavender's Greek Seasoning, and I used twice as much. Nice flavor. Sometimes I add 1/4 cup heavy cream at the end of cooking and let it sit 10 minutes--heavenly!! The family and teens eat this right up. Goes well with broiled fish or any meat dish.

I love this, especially with minor adjustments: I use brown rice because it's healthier, and Fideo instead of broken vermicelli. (Fideo is available in the Mexican food section.) I use 3.5 cups of water because brown rice needs more liquid and just a tad more chicken bouillon powder (Caldo de pollo is the best). I also add herbs de provence instead of greek seasoning. And simmer for about 45 minutes. We love it and leftovers freeze and reheat well.

I didn't have vermicelli so I used 1cup of rice only. I diced one medium onion and sauted it in 4 Tbsp. butter until translucent then added a heaping Tbsp. of minced garlic and sauted for one minute. After that I added 2 cups of Turkey broth and followed the recipe from there. It took about 20 minutes on low heat after bringing to a boil to cook through and absorb all the liquid. Very tasty rice dish. Served with baked chicken and kale. I will make this again.

Really good recipe for rice pilaf and easy to make! I subbed the vermicelli with gluten free thin spaghetti. I confused recipes and thought I needed ½ diced onion. So, I ended up sautéing it with the spaghetti. I used 2 cups homemade chicken broth instead of bouillon and water. I simply added a little of each spice (except for onion) from the Greek Seasoning recipe on this site. I also added about ¼ tsp turmeric because I wanted more of a yellow tint to the pilaf, which bouillon probably would have given. The only change I might make next time is to use 1/2 of the butter called for in the recipe, but that’s a personal preference. Recipe is excellent as written and we’ll definitely make it again. Thanks for the recipe!

Wow, pretty easy and good! As almost anything can be added to this great base, while it was simmering, in a site pan I did chopped onions, red pepper, and also some celery (which is is good for adding an earthiness flavor). I stirred it in after rice simmer was complete. Delicious. Amazing hw easy. Don’t be intimidated by frying vermicelli — it was my first time and it was easy. Adds amazing flavor to rice that rice so much more savory.

Very versitile, adjust the seasoning to fit the meal. I added leftover diced chicken to make a weeknight dinner. I would add the rice right after finishing the vermicelli to saute and coat the rice for a minute or two. Then add the liquid etc. Update: I substituted well washed basmati rice and cut 5 minutes off the cook time. Turned out outstanding.

I used brown rice and modified the recipe to account for the additional cooking time. About 50 minutes before serving I started a cup of brown rice with about 2 cups of water and chicken bouillon. About 30 minutes later, I used the butter to cook the small pasta pieces as recommended and then put them into the rice mixture, stirred and kept cooking until rice and pasta was tender. I also cooked some chopped onions and garlic with the pasta which is purely optional, but suits our love of vegetables.

What an absolutely delicious side dish for either chicken or pork. The store didn't have either vermicelli or greek seasoning. I used the greek seasoning recipe from the AR site (it was great) and whole grain thin spaghetti for the vermicelli. From a presentation perspective, I think I'll break the pasta into smaller pieces the next time. Since I used 2 tsp bouillon granules, I did not add the salt, and we didn't miss it. We like pepper, and this was just the perfect qty for us, but if you're not a pepper lover, you may want to approach that measurement cautiously. I think this would make an excellent filling for a hollowed out whole ripe summer tomato or even adding some shredded chicken to it for a summer lunch. Moist, flavorful, and just downright tasty. Thanks, Ann, this is a winner in my book.

I expected a nice side dish - but I hadn't expected the WOW. I didn't have vermicelli so I used orzo. I also used an extra long grain basmati rice (which I had rinsed first) . I will make it again using the orzo, it was a nice shape contrast. I had no store bought Greek spice so I followed a recipe I found online (I used fresh mint and fresh oregano). I added this pilaf to my permanent recipe book. So simple to prepare, yet tasted top chef. This is a spectacular recipe, thank you Ann.

I can't believe I haven't rated this recipe before now. I make it over and over and over. It is my go to rice dish. I had a recipe like it many years ago and somehow lost it. I was delighted to find this one.
My family loves this recipe! I sometimes sauté a small, diced onion along with the vermicelli.
Great recipe. I used a little less black pepper and a little more Greek seasoning.

This was quite easy to make and delicious! My husband loved it. I used homemade chicken broth and added some bouillon granules to that. I also used gluten free pasta because my husband has celiac and it still worked out great.
What would be the recipe for a crowd
Delicious, and I’ll never buy the boxed version again!! I did add just a bit more Greek Seasoning, and used chicken broth instead of the water and bouillon. This reheats very well.
Really good and easy to make especially if I'm busy cooking other items for a big meal.
